result.rationale: In parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts the keys `[z.string().toString()]` and `[z.string().optional().toString()]` both stringify to "[object Object]" (zod schemas don't override toString), so the second entry overwrites the first and the 'minimum' schema only guarantees access_token; zod's default strip mode then discards expiry_date/expires_in/instance_url etc. from sync-mode parse results. Callers in the diff (GoogleCalendarService, zoom, office365, salesforce) rely on those fields (e.g. `token.expiry_date`, `instance_url`), so the described data-loss mechanism is verifiable directly from the diff

judged_text: packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:8 — `[z.string().toString()]` and `[z.string().optional().toString()]` both evaluate to the same key "[object Object]", so the "minimum" schema is effectively `{access_token}` and zod strips every other field, meaning expiry (`expires_in`/`expiry_date`), `instance_url`, and the real `refresh_token` are discarded from every sync-mode parse result.
